## Statement

Let $V_k$ be locally bounded periodic interpolant extensions of finite nodal
arrays on grids with $h_k\to0$ and time steps $\tau_k\to0$. Regard this
sequence as the family $V_\epsilon=V_k$ when
$(k+1)^{-1}<\epsilon\le k^{-1}$, and form its upper and lower half-relaxed
limits as in
[[def-half-relaxed-limits]]. If $\overline V-\phi$ has a strict local maximum
at an interior point $z_0=(x_0,t_0)$ for a smooth test $\phi$, then there are
mesh indices $k_m\to\infty$ and grid points $z_m=(x_{i_m},t_{n_m})\to z_0$
such that $V_{k_m}(z_m)-\phi(z_m)\to\overline V(z_0)-\phi(z_0)$ and $z_m$ is
a local maximum of the corresponding nodal values minus $\phi$ on a fixed
closed space-time ball. The lower half-relaxed limit has the dual strict
minimum property. The proof uses Countable Choice only for sequential recovery
from the set-defined half-relaxed limit.

2.1 For all sufficiently large $m$, maximize the finite nonempty set of nodal values $U_i^n-\phi(x_i,t_n)$ inside $K$ and take its lexicographically first maximizing tuple $(i,n)$, comparing integer coordinates in displayed order and putting the smaller first differing coordinate first. A maximizer exists by [F3]; its value is at least the recovery value from step 1.2. Fix $r>0$ and let $A_r=K\setminus B_r(z_0)$. The strict gap $g_r$ from step 1.1 holds on $A_r$. For every $z\in A_r$, the set-based definition [F1] supplies a positive radius on which $V_\epsilon(y)\le\overline V(z)+g_r/8$ whenever both $\epsilon$ and $|y-z|$ are smaller than that radius. Continuity of $\phi$ and density of the positive rationals allow the following predicate on pairs $(z,q)$: $P_r(z,q)$ means $V_\epsilon(y)\le\overline V(z)+g_r/8$ for every $0<\epsilon<q$ and $|y-z|<q$, and $|\phi(y)-\phi(z)|<g_r/8$ for every $|y-z|<q$. The family $$\mathcal U_r=\{B(z,q/2):z\in A_r,\ q\in\mathbb Q_{>0},\ P_r(z,q)\}$$ is an open cover of $A_r$: for each center some real radius works by the relaxed-limit definition and continuity, and a smaller rational radius also works. This is the set of all qualifying rational pairs, not a choice of one radius for each $z$. By [F3] it has a finite subcover; let $q_*>0$ be the least radius in that finite subcover. Whenever $\epsilon<q_*$ and $y\in A_r$, a covering center gives $$V_\epsilon(y)-\phi(y)\le\overline V(z)-\phi(z)+g_r/4 \le\overline V(z_0)-\phi(z_0)-3g_r/4.$$ The recovery value in step 1.2 is eventually larger than this bound, so no maximizer on the grid in $K$ lies in $A_r$. Since this holds for every $r>0$, the maximizing nodes converge to $z_0$. Their values have lower limit at least the contact value by step 1.2; the upper-limit definition [F1], applied at these nodes, gives upper limit at most the same value. Thus their values converge to the upper half-relaxed contact value. [F1, F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability law.
For $G\in F^{k\times(k+p)}$ as in
[[lem-wide-gaussian-pseudoinverse-frobenius-moments]], put $X=\|G^\dagger\|_2$.
For $0<q<(p+1)/2$ over $\mathbb R$ and $0<q<p+1$ over normalized $\mathbb C$,
$$\mathbb E X^{2q}\le C_R(q):=\frac{2^{-q}\sqrt\pi\,\Gamma((p+1)/2-q)\Gamma(k/2+q)}{\Gamma((p+1)/2)\Gamma(k/2)\Gamma(q+1/2)},$$
$$\mathbb E X^{2q}\le C_C(q):=\frac{\Gamma(p+1-q)\Gamma(k+q)}{\Gamma(p+1)\Gamma(k)\Gamma(q+1)}.$$
For integers $p\ge2$, writing $\ell=k+p$ and $a=e\sqrt\ell/p$,
$$\mathbb E X^p\le a^p\quad(F=\mathbb R),\qquad \mathbb E X^{2p}\le a^{2p}\quad(F=\mathbb C).$$
Consequently $\mathbb E X\le a$ and
$$\mathbb P\{X>t\}\le\min(1,(a/t)^p)\quad(F=\mathbb R),\qquad \mathbb P\{X>t\}\le\min(1,(a/t)^{2p})\quad(F=\mathbb C),$$
for $t>0$. In the randomized range-finder application $p\ge2$, so these tails
are integrable at infinity.

1.1 If $h=0$, define $v$ arbitrarily; this event is null under the density [F9]. If $k=1$, then $|v_1|=1$ and both displayed sphere-moment formulas equal $1$. Suppose $k\ge2$. By the square laws and convolution derived in [F12], the independent variables $|h_1|^2$ and $\sum_{j=2}^k|h_j|^2$ have Gamma shapes $(1/2,(k-1)/2)$ and common scale $2$ over $\mathbb R$, and shapes $(1,k-1)$ and common scale $1$ over $\mathbb C$. Apply [F13] on the open positive quadrant using the inverse diffeomorphism $(s,t)\mapsto(x,y)=(st,s(1-t))$, with $s>0$, $0<t<1$ and absolute Jacobian $s$. In these coordinates the density factors into a Gamma$(a+b,\theta)$ factor in $s$ and a Beta$(a,b)$ factor in $t$ after scaling by the common scale $\theta$. Thus $\mathbb E t^q=B(a+q,b)/B(a,b)$; [F3] gives $c_R(q)=\Gamma(k/2)\Gamma(q+1/2)/(\sqrt\pi\Gamma(k/2+q))$ over $\mathbb R$ and $c_C(q)=\Gamma(k)\Gamma(q+1)/\Gamma(k+q)$ over $\mathbb C$. Invariance makes the same moment hold for $|\langle v,u\rangle|$ for every fixed unit $u$. [given, F2, F3, F6, F9, F12, F13, A1, choose]
cases.reason: The moment and tail estimates follow from reciprocal Gamma laws and invariant sphere integration.

## Example

Use root $H=[0,4]^2$; its two nonempty children are $P=[0,2]\times[0,2]$ and $Q=[2,4]\times[0,2]$. Name the lower children of $P$ by $C_0=[0,1]\times[0,1]$ and $C=[1,2]\times[0,1]$. Name the lower-left, lower-right, and upper-left children of $Q$ by $D_0=[2,3]\times[0,1]$, $D=[3,4]\times[0,1]$, and $D_1=[2,3]\times[1,2]$; its upper-right child and the two upper root children are empty. Let leaf threshold $s=2$ and split each cell with more than two labels. Put unit charges at $c\pm\tfrac14$ in $C$, where $c=\tfrac32+\tfrac12i$, a charge $3$ at $d-0.1$ in $D$, where $d=\tfrac72+\tfrac12i$, and a zero-charge target label at $d$. Put zero-charge labels at $\tfrac12+\tfrac12i$ in $C_0$, $\tfrac52+\tfrac12i$ in $D_0$, and $\tfrac52+\tfrac32i$ in $D_1$. Then $P$ has three labels and $Q$ has four, so both split and their named grandchildren are leaves. For the target $d$, the recursion records $(C,D)$ as far and the charge-$3$ pair in $D$ as direct near. Use the analytic logarithm on the far difference disk that is real at $2$; the near difference $0.1$ uses its real logarithm. Take order $p=1$.

1.1 The root has seven labels, and its nonempty children $P,Q$ have three and four labels, respectively; threshold $s=2$ therefore splits all three, while the named grandchildren are leaves. The centers of $P,Q$ are $1+i,3+i$, their radii are $\sqrt2$, and their center distance is $2<2\sqrt2$, so $(P,Q)$ is not separated. The tie rule splits source $P$, exposing $C$ with center $c=3/2+i/2$ and radius $\sqrt2/2$. The pair $(C,Q)$ is not separated since its center distance is $\sqrt{5/2}<3\sqrt2/2$, so the larger target cell $Q$ is split. The child $D$ has center $d=7/2+i/2$ and radius $\sqrt2/2$, and $|d-c|=2>\sqrt2$; hence $(C,D)$ is far. The distinct charge-$3$ source and zero-charge target at $d$ lie in the same leaf $D$, so their ordered pair is direct near. [given, F1, algebra]
cases.evidence: The target is strictly inside its named leaf and its direct near separation is the nonzero real number one tenth.

## Definition

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\alpha<2$, put $\rho=1-\alpha>-1$, and let $n\ge1$. For a continuous amplitude $G$ on $[0,1]^2$, let $(z_j,w_j)_{j=1}^n$ be the Gauss–Jacobi rule for weight $(1+t)^\rho$ on $[-1,1]$, and $(\zeta_i,v_i)_{i=1}^n$ the rule for weight $1$ there. Map nodes and weights to $[0,1]$ by
$$r_j=(1+z_j)/2,\quad a_j=2^{-(\rho+1)}w_j,\qquad s_i=(1+\zeta_i)/2,\quad b_i=v_i/2.$$
The **Duffy weighted product rule** is
$$Q_{n,\alpha}^{D}(G)=\sum_{j=1}^n\sum_{i=1}^n a_jb_iG(r_j,s_i).$$
It approximates $\int_0^1\int_0^1r^{1-\alpha}G(r,s)\,ds\,dr$, the transformed integral of [[thm-duffy-weak-singularity-transform]]. The finite nodes and weights are well-defined by the supplied Gauss–Jacobi rule; the error estimate is [[cor-duffy-weighted-product-gauss-error]].

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge1$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be
a bounded open set, let $1<p<\infty$ satisfy
$p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$, and let $T>0$. Let $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$
with gradient norm, $H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and let
$a(x,\xi)$ satisfy [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]]. Assume an admissible
stable conforming FEM sequence $(V_k,\Pi_k,\mathcal P_k)$ from
[[def-pe12-stable-conforming-fem-family]]. For $f\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$ and
$u_0\in H$, set $f_k^n=|I_k^n|^{-1}\int_{I_k^n}f$ and $U_k^0=\Pi_ku_0$.
For each $k$, let $(U_k^n)$ be any solution of the backward Euler equations
in [[thm-pe12-backward-euler-galerkin-existence-energy]].

There are a subsequence, still indexed by $k$, and a unique
$u\in L^p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)\cap C([0,T];H)$ such that
$$\overline U_k\to u\quad\text{strongly in }L^r(0,T;H) \text{ for every }1\le r<\infty,\qquad \overline U_k\rightharpoonup u\text{ in }L^p(0,T;V),$$
the fluxes $a(x,\nabla\overline U_k)$ converge weakly in
$L^{p'}((0,T)\times\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ to $a(x,\nabla u)$, and
$$u'+A(u)=f\quad\text{in }L^{p'}(0,T;V^*),\qquad u(0)=u_0.$$
Existence of each discrete solution and uniform energy bounds are included
in [[thm-pe12-backward-euler-galerkin-existence-energy]]. The abstract
convergence claim is conditional on the FEM projector clauses. For
$\Omega=(0,1)$ in $d=1$ and $\Omega=(0,1)^d$ in each $d\ge2$, the explicit
fixed-degree interval and Kuhn/Freudenthal simplex families of
[[thm-pe12-l2-projector-w1p-stability]] verify those clauses for any
independent time partitions with vanishing maximum step. These are concrete
nonempty instances of the theorem on the full approved strict $p$ range.

9.1 For the unit interval in $d=1$, [F13] supplies the projector sequence for every $p>1$, which is the stated strict threshold. For the unit cube in any $d\ge2$, [F13] supplies it for every $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$. Choose any time partitions with maximum step tending to zero, independently of the spatial index. The resulting mesh/projector/time sequences satisfy every hypothesis used in the preceding convergence proof, so the abstract convergence and uniqueness conclusion holds on these explicit nonempty standard-mesh families without an additional projector assumption. [F13, given, step 1.1, step 1.3] ∎

## Definition

Let $\Omega$ be a bounded contractible Lipschitz polyhedron with a finite matching affine tetrahedral mesh $\mathcal T_h$, and use the real lowest-order spaces $W_h^0,N_h^1,N_h^2,N_h^3$ defined in [[def-na-lowest-order-whitney-de-rham-spaces]]. The electric trial field is $E_h(t)\in N_h^1\cap H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$; the magnetic flux field is $B_h(t)\in N_h^2$, with no imposed zero normal trace on $B_h$. PEC means the closure-defined zero tangential subspace from [[def-na-zero-tangential-hcurl]]. Periodic analogues use the periodic cell complex. Countable Choice is inherited from the H(div) and affine Piola space definitions in the suppliers; the finite matrix operations below use no additional choice.

Put $V_h:=N_h^1\cap H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$. Choose an edge basis $\{\phi_i\}_{i=1}^{N_e}$ of the electric trial space $V_h$ and a face basis $\{\psi_a\}_{a=1}^{N_f}$ of $N_h^2$, so $N_e=\dim V_h$ and $N_f=\dim N_h^2$. Define the symmetric mass matrices
$$ (M_e)_{ij}=\int_\Omega \phi_j^T\epsilon\phi_i\,dx,\qquad (M_b)_{ab}=\int_\Omega \psi_b^T\mu^{-1}\psi_a\,dx.$$
They are positive definite by the coefficient bounds in [[def-transient-maxwell-system-with-material-interfaces]] and linear independence of the finite element bases. Let $C$ and $D$ be the coefficient matrices, in these chosen bases, of the restricted map $\operatorname{curl}:V_h\to N_h^2$ and of $\operatorname{div}:N_h^2\to N_h^3$. The moment-commuting supplier gives $DC=0$ on the full spaces, hence also after restriction to $V_h$. Set $j_i(t)=\int_\Omega J_{\rm src}(t)\cdot\phi_i\,dx$, with $J_{\rm src}\in C([0,T];L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3))$. The lossless, conductivity-free semidiscretization with this source is
$$M_e\dot e-C^TM_b b=-j,\qquad \dot b+Ce=0.$$
This is a spatial Galerkin system only; no time integrator is included. The cochain convention and weak material-interface formulation come from the declared spaces and [[def-transient-maxwell-system-with-material-interfaces]]. Smooth interpolation and a uniformly bounded commuting projection are separate prerequisites for the later error estimate and are not asserted by this definition.

For the incidence matrices $G,C,D$ of [[def-maxwell-discrete-cochain-and-yee-grid]], one has $CG=0$ and $DC=0$. The conclusion holds for the full periodic complex and for the PEC mixed closure defined there.

2.1 Periodic identification identifies faces with the prescribed orientation, so the quotient cell structure retains oriented boundary-of-boundary cancellation. For PEC, let $\bar G,\bar C,\bar D$ be the absolute incidence matrices and let $P_e$ select interior edges and $P_v$ select interior vertices. The matrices are $G=P_e\bar G P_v$, $C=\bar C P_e^T$, and $D=\bar D$. An interior vertex is incident to no boundary edge, so $P_e^TP_e\bar G P_v=\bar G P_v$. Hence $CG=\bar C\bar G P_v=0$, while $DC=\bar D\bar C P_e^T=0$. This retains boundary-face magnetic cochains although boundary electric edge values are fixed. [F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Definition

Use the spaces and partial Schur operator of [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and [[def-pe26-discrete-harmonic-extension-and-schur-complement]]. Let $E_0:\widetilde W\to\widehat W$ average every remaining interface degree of freedom and preserve every already-shared primal value. It is a scaled average if the weights for all copies of each such degree of freedom sum to one. Put $\bar E:=R E_0:\widetilde W\to\widetilde W$. Then $E_0R=I_{\widehat W}$ and $\bar E$ is a projection onto $\widehat W$.

In the PE26 two-dimensional corner-constraint branch, each non-primal node is interior to one interface edge shared by exactly two subdomains $i,j$. Set

$$ (E_0w)(x)=\frac{\rho_i}{\rho_i+\rho_j}w_i(x)+\frac{\rho_j}{\rho_i+\rho_j}w_j(x). $$

At primal nodes the copies already agree, so the average is the common value. For any finite-dimensional positive definite partial Schur operator $\widetilde S$, the **BDDC preconditioner** is

$$M_{\rm BDDC}^{-1}:=E_0\widetilde S^{-1}E_0^T:\widehat W'\to\widehat W,$$

for the assembled interface system with operator $\widehat S=R^T\widetilde S R$. Its constrained partial-energy interpretation is established in [[prop-pe26-bddc-constrained-local-minimization]].
cases.evidence: When there are no remaining interface degrees of freedom the averaging map acts on the zero space and the formulas are vacuous.

## Statement

The flux in [[def-ideal-gas-entropy-conservative-pair-flux]] is well-defined for every pair in $\mathcal G\times\mathcal G$, symmetric in its two states, and consistent in the sense that $F_j^{\mathrm{ec}}(U,U)=F_j(U)$. It satisfies

$$(v(U_R)-v(U_L))^TF_j^{\mathrm{ec}}(U_L,U_R)=\psi_j(U_R)-\psi_j(U_L).$$

The flux is locally Lipschitz on $\mathcal G\times\mathcal G$.

1.1 If $U_L=U_R$, then $\Delta v=0$ and [F1] gives $F_j^{\mathrm{ec}}(U_L,U_R)=F_j(U_L)$. If $U_L\ne U_R$, convexity [F3] keeps the segment $U(t)=U_L+t(U_R-U_L)$ in $\mathcal G$, and $\Delta v^T(U_R-U_L)=\int_0^1 (U_R-U_L)^TD_U^2\eta(U(t))(U_R-U_L)\,dt>0$ by [F2]. Hence $\Delta v\ne0$, so the denominator in [F1] is nonzero; also $\bar U\in\mathcal G$. This proves well-definedness and consistency. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]
cases.reason: Each ideal-gas input state lies in the positive-density positive-internal-energy domain.

## Statement

The flux in [[def-ideal-gas-entropy-conservative-pair-flux]] is well-defined for every pair in $\mathcal G\times\mathcal G$, symmetric in its two states, and consistent in the sense that $F_j^{\mathrm{ec}}(U,U)=F_j(U)$. It satisfies

1.3 Fix a state $X\in\mathcal G$ and write $U_R=X+h/2$, $U_L=X-h/2$ for small $h$. The entropy compatibility in [F2] implies $D_U\psi_j(X)=F_j(X)^TD_Uv(X)$. Symmetric Taylor expansions therefore give $\Delta v=D_Uv(X)h+O(|h|^3)$ and $\Delta\psi_j=F_j(X)^TD_Uv(X)h+O(|h|^3)$, so $N:=\Delta\psi_j-\Delta v^TF_j(X)=O(|h|^3)$. Positive definiteness of $D_Uv(X)$ implies $|\Delta v|\ge c|h|$ in a sufficiently small neighborhood of $h=0$. [F2, algebra]

## Statement

For fixed $\varepsilon>0$, odd grid size $N$, and $Q,M$ as in [[def-periodic-pic-regularized-grid-interaction-kernel]], define
$$ M_x^{\varepsilon,h}=\sup_{x,y\in\mathbb T_L^d}\|D_x(cQ\mathcal E_{\varepsilon,h})(x,y)\|_{\rm op},\qquad M_y^{\varepsilon,h}=\sup_{x,y\in\mathbb T_L^d}\|D_y(cQ\mathcal E_{\varepsilon,h})(x,y)\|_{\rm op} $$ and $L_{\varepsilon,h}=\max\{1,M_x^{\varepsilon,h},M_y^{\varepsilon,h}\}$. These are finite mesh- and regularization-dependent constants. The phase kernel $\mathbb K_{\varepsilon,h}$ is globally Lipschitz in the two-variable convention $$ |\mathbb K_{\varepsilon,h}(z,z')-\mathbb K_{\varepsilon,h}(\widetilde z,\widetilde z')| \le L_{\varepsilon,h}\bigl(|z-\widetilde z|+|z'-\widetilde z'|\bigr). $$ The continuum kernel $\mathbb K_\varepsilon$ is also globally Lipschitz with the explicit admissible constant $$ L_\varepsilon=\max\left\{1,\frac{|cQ|}{L^d} \sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{0\}}\prod_{a=1}^d\alpha_\varepsilon^{2|k_a|}\right\}. $$

1.1 By [F2], each grid weight is smooth and has bounded derivatives of every finite order. By [F1], $\mathcal E_{\varepsilon,h}$ is a finite sum of products of such weights and fixed matrix entries, so it is $C^\infty$ and all its derivatives are bounded. In particular, both derivative suprema $M_x^{\varepsilon,h},M_y^{\varepsilon,h}$ are finite. More explicitly, if $B_{jk}$ are the vector entries of $-D^0A_h^\dagger$ and $C_w=\max_j\|\nabla w_j\|_\infty$, then $M_x^{\varepsilon,h}\le |cQ|h^{-d}C_w \sum_{j,k}|B_{jk}|\|w_k\|_\infty,\qquad M_y^{\varepsilon,h}\le |cQ|h^{-d}C_w \sum_{j,k}|B_{jk}|\|w_j\|_\infty ,$ which are finite explicit bounds for the defining suprema. ## Statement

For every $k,R>0$ and smooth $g$ on $\mathbb S^2$, the series in [[def-pe18-exact-spherical-dtn-map]] converges in $C^\infty(\mathbb S^2)$ to $T_{k,R}g$, and $|\tau_\ell(k,R)|\le k+(\ell+1)/R$. Its outgoing extension converges in $C^2$ on each compact annulus $R\le r\le R_1$, solves $(\Delta+k^2)v=0$, has trace $v(R,\cdot)=g$ and radial derivative $\partial_rv(R,\cdot)=T_{k,R}g$, and satisfies the uniform outgoing Sommerfeld condition as $r\to\infty$. It is the unique classical outgoing extension of $g$.

1.1 By [F3], $|\tau_\ell|\le k+(\ell+1)/R$. The $C^p$ estimate in [F5] and the super-polynomial decay in [F2] show that for every $p$, $\sum_\ell\|\tau_\ell g_\ell\|_{C^p}<\infty$. Thus the defining series converges in every smooth norm to a smooth function $T_{k,R}g$. [F2, F3, F5, algebra]

## Statement

Let $X_c$ and $X_d$ be the stabilizing CARE and DARE solutions under the hypotheses of [[thm-care-stabilizing-psd-solution-and-value]] and [[thm-dare-stabilizing-psd-solution-and-value]]. Their residual derivatives on Hermitian matrices are
$$\mathcal L_c(E)=A_c(X_c)^*E+EA_c(X_c),\qquad \mathcal L_d(E)=A_c(X_d)^*EA_c(X_d)-E.$$
When invertible, the local residual condition numbers are $\kappa_c=\|\mathcal L_c^{-1}\|_{F\to F}$ and $\kappa_d=\|\mathcal L_d^{-1}\|_{F\to F}$. If additive Hermitian residual perturbations admit radii satisfying the contraction and separate stability-margin hypotheses of [[thm-care-local-residual-ball-certificate]] or [[thm-dare-local-residual-ball-certificate]], the perturbed equations have stabilizing roots within those radii; the linear leading sensitivity is $-\mathcal L_c^{-1}\Delta$ or $-\mathcal L_d^{-1}\Delta$.

For CARE, write $T_X=\begin{bmatrix}I&0\\X_c&I\end{bmatrix}$ and let $\sigma=\operatorname{sep}(-A_c(X_c)^*,A_c(X_c))>0$, with $\kappa_s=1/\sigma$. For a Hamiltonian perturbation $\Delta H$, put $Z=T_X^{-1}\Delta H T_X$, $\zeta=\|Z\|_F$, $\theta=\kappa_s\zeta$, and $\mu=\kappa_s\|G\|_2$. If $6\theta+4\mu\theta+4\theta^2<1$, the perturbed Hamiltonian has an invariant graph $\operatorname{Ran}[I;X_c+Y]$ with $\|Y\|_F\le2\theta$. If its restriction is certified Hurwitz and the perturbed Hamiltonian is certified to have exactly $n$ left-half-plane eigenvalues, this graph is its stable subspace.

Finally, for either an exact CARE invariant graph basis or DARE deflating graph basis $U=[U_1;U_2]$ with invertible $U_1$, let $X=U_2U_1^{-1}$ and let $\widetilde U=U+\Delta U$. If $\|U_1^{-1}\|_2\|\Delta U_1\|_2<1$, then $\widetilde U_1$ remains invertible and
$$\|\widetilde U_2\widetilde U_1^{-1}-X\|_2\le\frac{\|\Delta U_2\|_2+\|X\|_2\|\Delta U_1\|_2}{\|U_1^{-1}\|_2^{-1}-\|\Delta U_1\|_2}.$$

## Statement

$$\mathcal L_c(E)=A_c(X_c)^*E+EA_c(X_c),\qquad \mathcal L_d(E)=A_c(X_d)^*EA_c(X_d)-E.$$
When invertible, the local residual condition numbers are $\kappa_c=\|\mathcal L_c^{-1}\|_{F\to F}$ and $\kappa_d=\|\mathcal L_d^{-1}\|_{F\to F}$. If additive Hermitian residual perturbations admit radii satisfying the contraction and separate stability-margin hypotheses of [[thm-care-local-residual-ball-certificate]] or [[thm-dare-local-residual-ball-certificate]], the perturbed equations have stabilizing roots within those radii; the linear leading sensitivity is $-\mathcal L_c^{-1}\Delta$ or $-\mathcal L_d^{-1}\Delta$.

For a Hamiltonian perturbation $\Delta H$, put $Z=T_X^{-1}\Delta H T_X$, $\zeta=\|Z\|_F$, $\theta=\kappa_s\zeta$, and $\mu=\kappa_s\|G\|_2$. If $6\theta+4\mu\theta+4\theta^2<1$, the perturbed Hamiltonian has an invariant graph $\operatorname{Ran}[I;X_c+Y]$ with $\|Y\|_F\le2\theta$. If its restriction is certified Hurwitz and the perturbed Hamiltonian is certified to have exactly $n$ left-half-plane eigenvalues, this graph is its stable subspace.

Finally, for either an exact CARE invariant graph basis or DARE deflating graph basis $U=[U_1;U_2]$ with invertible $U_1$, let $X=U_2U_1^{-1}$ and let $\widetilde U=U+\Delta U$. If $\|U_1^{-1}\|_2\|\Delta U_1\|_2<1$, then $\widetilde U_1$ remains invertible and
$$\|\widetilde U_2\widetilde U_1^{-1}-X\|_2\le\frac{\|\Delta U_2\|_2+\|X\|_2\|\Delta U_1\|_2}{\|U_1^{-1}\|_2^{-1}-\|\Delta U_1\|_2}.$$
This basis-chart estimate does not by itself certify a perturbed QZ deflating subspace.

For the DARE pencil, [[prop-dare-stable-deflating-subspace-perturbation-bound]] gives a separate perturbation-to-stable-deflating-space estimate from a generalized Sylvester separation, explicit contraction inequalities, and distinct leading/trailing Stein margins. Under those conditions its aligned orthonormal stable basis changes by at most $\beta(r)\le r$. The computable physical chart estimate additionally requires $\|U_1^{-1}\|_2\beta(r)<1$; without that margin the chart remains inconclusive. A QZ pencil backward-error bound alone supplies none of these conditions.

2.1 For a CARE additive residual perturbation $\Delta$, write $X=X_c+E$ and let $\delta=\|\Delta\|_F$. Then $F_c(X_c)=0$ and step 1.1 makes the perturbed root equation equivalent to $E=-\mathcal L_c^{-1}\Delta+\mathcal L_c^{-1}(EGE).$ If $\rho$ satisfies $\kappa_c(\delta+\|G\|_2\rho^2)\le\rho$ and $2\kappa_c\|G\|_2\rho<1$, the map sends the closed radius-$\rho$ Hermitian ball to itself and has Lipschitz constant at most the second displayed quantity. Iteration from zero gives geometric successive differences; [F10] gives a limit in the ball, continuity gives a fixed point, and contraction gives uniqueness. Let $W_c=\int_0^\infty e^{tA_c^*}e^{tA_c}\,dt\succ0$; then $A_c^*W_c+W_cA_c=-I$. If also $2\|W_c\|_2\|G\|_2\rho<1$, then $\|EGW_c+W_cGE\|_2\le2\|W_c\|_2\|G\|_2\rho<1$. Hence $(A_c-GE)^*W_c+W_c(A_c-GE)\prec0$; an eigenvector $v$ with eigenvalue $\lambda$ gives $2\operatorname{Re}(\lambda)v^*W_cv<0$, so the perturbed loop is Hurwitz. For DARE, [F2] gives Schur stability and [F11] gives the Stein inverse $\mathcal L_d^{-1}(Y)=-\sum_{k\ge0}(A_c^*)^kYA_c^k$. On a sufficiently small ball, $S(X)=R+B^*XB\succeq\delta_S I$, where $\delta_S=\lambda_{\min}S(X_d)-b^2\rho>0$. Put $a=\|A\|_2$, $b=\|B\|_2$, and $m=\|X_d\|_F+\rho$. The resolvent identity gives $\|S(X)^{-1}\|_2\le\delta_S^{-1}$ and $\|S(X)^{-1}-S(Y)^{-1}\|_2\le b^2\delta_S^{-2}\|X-Y\|_F$. Splitting $K(X)-K(Y)$ into its $X$ and inverse-factor changes yields $\|K(X)-K(Y)\|_F\le L_K\|X-Y\|_F$, where $L_K=ab/\delta_S+ab^3m/\delta_S^2$; hence $\|A_c(X)\|_2\le M_c=a+ab^2m/\delta_S$ and $\|A_c(X)-A_c(Y)\|_2\le L_c\|X-Y\|_F$, $L_c=bL_K$. ## Statement

$$\mathcal L_c(E)=A_c(X_c)^*E+EA_c(X_c),\qquad \mathcal L_d(E)=A_c(X_d)^*EA_c(X_d)-E.$$
When invertible, the local residual condition numbers are $\kappa_c=\|\mathcal L_c^{-1}\|_{F\to F}$ and $\kappa_d=\|\mathcal L_d^{-1}\|_{F\to F}$. If additive Hermitian residual perturbations admit radii satisfying the contraction and separate stability-margin hypotheses of [[thm-care-local-residual-ball-certificate]] or [[thm-dare-local-residual-ball-certificate]], the perturbed equations have stabilizing roots within those radii; the linear leading sensitivity is $-\mathcal L_c^{-1}\Delta$ or $-\mathcal L_d^{-1}\Delta$.

For CARE, write $T_X=\begin{bmatrix}I&0\\X_c&I\end{bmatrix}$ and let $\sigma=\operatorname{sep}(-A_c(X_c)^*,A_c(X_c))>0$, with $\kappa_s=1/\sigma$. For a Hamiltonian perturbation $\Delta H$, put $Z=T_X^{-1}\Delta H T_X$, $\zeta=\|Z\|_F$, $\theta=\kappa_s\zeta$, and $\mu=\kappa_s\|G\|_2$. If $6\theta+4\mu\theta+4\theta^2<1$, the perturbed Hamiltonian has an invariant graph $\operatorname{Ran}[I;X_c+Y]$ with $\|Y\|_F\le2\theta$. If its restriction is certified Hurwitz and the perturbed Hamiltonian is certified to have exactly $n$ left-half-plane eigenvalues, this graph is its stable subspace.

Finally, for either an exact CARE invariant graph basis or DARE deflating graph basis $U=[U_1;U_2]$ with invertible $U_1$, let $X=U_2U_1^{-1}$ and let $\widetilde U=U+\Delta U$. If $\|U_1^{-1}\|_2\|\Delta U_1\|_2<1$, then $\widetilde U_1$ remains invertible and
$$\|\widetilde U_2\widetilde U_1^{-1}-X\|_2\le\frac{\|\Delta U_2\|_2+\|X\|_2\|\Delta U_1\|_2}{\|U_1^{-1}\|_2^{-1}-\|\Delta U_1\|_2}.$$
This basis-chart estimate does not by itself certify a perturbed QZ deflating subspace.

For the DARE pencil, [[prop-dare-stable-deflating-subspace-perturbation-bound]] gives a separate perturbation-to-stable-deflating-space estimate from a generalized Sylvester separation, explicit contraction inequalities, and distinct leading/trailing Stein margins. Under those conditions its aligned orthonormal stable basis changes by at most $\beta(r)\le r$. The computable physical chart estimate additionally requires $\|U_1^{-1}\|_2\beta(r)<1$; without that margin the chart remains inconclusive. A QZ pencil backward-error bound alone supplies none of these conditions.

Direct multiplication gives $\Phi_G(X+E)-\Phi_G(X)=(I+(X+E)G)^{-1}E(I+GX)^{-1},\quad \Phi_G(X)=X(I+GX)^{-1}.$ Taking the derivative at $E=0$ and multiplying by $A^*,A$ gives $Df(X)[E]=A_c(X)^*EA_c(X)$; since $F_d=f-X$, this gives $DF_d(X)[E]=A_c(X)^*EA_c(X)-E$. [F3, given, algebra]

## Example

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, and additionally assume Dependent Choice $\mathrm{DC}$ when $u_0\in L^1(\mathbb R)$.

Let $I=[a_-,a_+]$ be a compact invariant interval, let $f\in C^1(\mathbb R)$,
and choose finite $L,\alpha$ with $|f'(s)|\le L$ on $I$ and $\alpha\ge L$.
The Lax–Friedrichs flux
$$F_{\mathrm{LF}}(a,b):=\frac{f(a)+f(b)}2-\frac\alpha2(b-a)$$
is consistent, nondecreasing in $a$, nonincreasing in $b$, and has coordinate
Lipschitz bounds $L_1=L_2=(L+\alpha)/2$. Thus any bounded BV datum in $I$ and
mesh family satisfying
$$\frac{\tau_m}{h_m}(L+\alpha)\le1,\qquad \frac{\tau_m}{h_m}\ge c_*>0,\qquad h_m,\tau_m\to0$$
falls under [[thm-monotone-finite-volume-entropy-convergence]].

1.1 On the diagonal, $F_{\mathrm{LF}}(s,s)=f(s)$, so the flux is consistent. If $a_2=a_1$, the first-coordinate difference is zero; if $a_2>a_1$, the mean-value theorem gives $F_{\mathrm{LF}}(a_2,b)-F_{\mathrm{LF}}(a_1,b)=\frac{f(a_2)-f(a_1)+\alpha(a_2-a_1)}2\ge\frac{\alpha-L}{2}(a_2-a_1)\ge0.$ Thus it is nondecreasing in its first coordinate. [F1, F2, given, algebra]
cases.reason: Coordinate monotonicity and the stated CFL inequality verify the hypotheses of the finite-volume convergence supplier.

## Statement

Let $h_{k,j}\to0$, $\tau_k=T/M_k\to0$, and let $U_k$ be the finite
solutions of [[alg-na-explicit-diagonal-diffusion-hjb-grid-step]] with its
diffusion-dominance and CFL inequalities at every row. Extend each array
multilinearly in space, constantly on each time interval, and by its initial
interpolant for $-1<t<0$; identify the mesh sequence with the parameter
family convention of [[def-half-relaxed-limits]]. Its upper
half-relaxed limit is a bounded upper semicontinuous viscosity subsolution,
and its lower half-relaxed limit is a bounded lower semicontinuous viscosity
supersolution of the periodic diagonal-diffusion Cauchy problem, with the
respective relaxed initial inequalities equal to $u_0$. This is a stability
statement only; it does not claim that the two limits coincide.

1.1 The row weights in [F1] give $$\|U_k^n\|_\infty\le\|u_0\|_\infty+n\tau_kF \le\|u_0\|_\infty+TF.$$ Multilinear interpolation is a convex combination, so the same bound holds for the space-time extensions. They are locally bounded and their half-relaxed limits have the semicontinuity and order properties in [F6]. [F1, F6, given, algebra]

## Statement

Let $h_{k,j}\to0$, $\tau_k=T/M_k\to0$, and let $U_k$ be the finite
solutions of [[alg-na-explicit-diagonal-diffusion-hjb-grid-step]] with its
diffusion-dominance and CFL inequalities at every row. Extend each array
multilinearly in space, constantly on each time interval, and by its initial
interpolant for $-1<t<0$; identify the mesh sequence with the parameter
family convention of [[def-half-relaxed-limits]]. Its upper
half-relaxed limit is a bounded upper semicontinuous viscosity subsolution,
and its lower half-relaxed limit is a bounded lower semicontinuous viscosity
supersolution of the periodic diagonal-diffusion Cauchy problem, with the
respective relaxed initial inequalities equal to $u_0$. This is a stability
statement only; it does not claim that the two limits coincide.

2.1 Let $\overline U-\phi$ have a local maximum at $(x_0,t_0)$, with $0<t_0<T$ and smooth $\phi$. Add $\varepsilon(|x-x_0|^4+|t-t_0|^4)$ to $\phi$; this makes the contact strict without changing its derivatives used by the PDE at $(x_0,t_0)$, as in [F4]. Select nodal local maxima $(x_k,t_k)$ from [F3] and put $c_k=U_{i_k}^{n_k}-\phi(x_k,t_k)$. All coordinate neighbors used by the explicit stencil at the previous time lie in the fixed contact cylinder for sufficiently large $k$, because their distance to $(x_k,t_k)$ is at most $h_{k,\max}+\tau_k$. Thus $U_j^{n_k-1}\le\phi(x_j,t_k-\tau_k)+c_k$ at every stencil node. Monotonicity and shift invariance in [F1] give $$U_{i_k}^{n_k}=S_k(U^{n_k-1})_{i_k} \le S_k(\phi(\cdot,t_k-\tau_k)+c_k)_{i_k} =S_k(\phi(\cdot,t_k-\tau_k))_{i_k}+c_k.$$ At the contact node $U_{i_k}^{n_k}=\phi(x_k,t_k)+c_k$, so the normalized residual is nonpositive. Passing to the limit by [F2] yields $$\phi_t-\max_a\{\sum_j(\alpha_j^a\phi_{x_jx_j}+b_j^a\phi_{x_j})+f^a\}\le0$$ at $(x_0,t_0)$. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]
cases.evidence: Degenerate parabolic coefficients are permitted by nonnegative row weights; no inverse elliptic coefficient is used.

## Statement

Let $0<\delta<1/4$, take the one-dimensional type-1 data
$$x_0=1/4,\qquad x_1=1/4+\delta,\qquad c_0=1,\quad c_1=-1,$$
and include mode $k=1$. For every real $\delta$ in this range, $\|c\|_1=2$ while
$$F_1=e^{-\pi i/2}(1-e^{-2\pi i\delta}),\qquad |F_1|\le2\pi\delta.$$
Thus this exact Fourier coefficient tends to zero as the source points cluster, although the coefficient l1 norm remains $2$. The dyadic subfamily, for example $\delta=2^{-n}$ with $n\ge3$, consists of admissible exact input coordinates and also tends to zero. For any such dyadic datum for which the algorithm has a successful run, the theorem gives an absolute l1-scaled error certificate; the exact family has no positive lower bound on $|F_1|$ from which that certificate alone yields a relative-error guarantee.

1.1 Since $c_0=1$ and $c_1=-1$, [F7] gives $\|c\|_1=|1|+|-1|=2$. For mode $1$, substitute the source locations into [F1] to obtain $F_1=e^{-2\pi i/4}-e^{-2\pi i(1/4+\delta)}=e^{-\pi i/2}(1-e^{-2\pi i\delta}).$ This is a direct factorization of the exact two-term sum. [given, F1, F7, algebra]
cases.reason: Exactly two labeled sources are supplied, so the cluster example is not an empty source sum.

## Statement

Let $0<\delta<1/4$, take the one-dimensional type-1 data
$$x_0=1/4,\qquad x_1=1/4+\delta,\qquad c_0=1,\quad c_1=-1,$$
and include mode $k=1$. For every real $\delta$ in this range, $\|c\|_1=2$ while

2.1 Put $t=\pi\delta$. By the complex exponential addition law and [F3], $1-e^{-2it}=e^{-it}(e^{it}-e^{-it})=e^{-it}(2i\sin t),$ so $|1-e^{-2it}|=2|\sin t|$ by [F3] and [F8]. From [F3]–[F5], for $t\ge0$ we have $|\sin t|=\left|\int_0^t\cos s\,ds\right|\le t\max_{0\le s\le t}|\cos s|\le t.$ Since $t=\pi\delta>0$ by [F6] and $|e^{-\pi i/2}|=1$, step 1.1 yields $|F_1|\le2t=2\pi\delta$. Taking the dyadic sequence $\delta=2^{-n}$ with $n\ge3$ shows that admissible exact input coefficients can have $|F_1|$ arbitrarily small while step 1.1 keeps $\|c\|_1=2$ by [F7]. Whenever a successful run is available for one of these inputs, [F2] gives an absolute bound without division by $|F_1|$; thus the certificate alone supplies no uniform relative-error estimate without an additional lower bound on the exact output. [A1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability law.
Let $A\in F^{m\times n}$ be fixed, where $F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$. Let
$k\ge2$, $p\ge2$, $\ell=k+p\le\min(m,n)$, and draw $\Omega$ with iid
standard real entries if $F=\mathbb R$ or normalized complex entries if
$F=\mathbb C$. If $Q$ is an orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{Ran}(A\Omega)$,
then
$$\mathbb E\|A-QQ^*A\|_2\le \left(1+\sqrt{\frac{k}{p-1}}\right)\sigma_{k+1} +\frac{e\sqrt{k+p}}{p}\left(\sum_{j>k}\sigma_j^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
This preserves the normalized-complex convention $\mathbb E|\Omega_{ij}|^2=1$.
1.1 If $F=\mathbb R$, the hypotheses and constants are exactly those of [F1], which proves the asserted expectation bound. [given, F1]

## Definition

Inputs are an exact dyadic complex number $z$, a target label
$\operatorname{Ai}$ or $\operatorname{Bi}$, positive rational absolute
tolerance $\varepsilon_a$, optional positive rational relative tolerance
$\varepsilon_r$, a fixed exponent range $(e_{\min},e_{\max})$, and finite
positive integer caps $S_{\max},K_{\max},p_{\max},W$, with $p_{\max}\ge2$.
Reject an invalid target, nonpositive tolerance, invalid cap, or
$e_{\min}>e_{\max}$ with domain. The caps bound stages,
terms per residue class, final dyadic precision, and this procedure's exact
interval operations and subroutine calls. For stage $q$, use $K=q$,
precision $p=\max(2,\min(q,p_{\max}))$, and elementary-range truncation $q$;
run stages $q=1,\ldots,\min(S_{\max},K_{\max},p_{\max})$.

All arithmetic uses [[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]].
Charge every exact arithmetic operation, range-evaluator node operation,
term, rounding, and loop update to the shared counter $W$. Return
inconclusive before any local operation would exceed $W$; interrupt a nested
subroutine before its next operation would exceed the remaining budget. When
nested, charge every Gamma-child operation directly to the same parent counter.
If a final
endpoint overflows, return range. A non-finite subroutine result makes the
current stage unavailable; later stages may still be tried. Other statuses
are those of [[def-certified-evaluation-result-contract]].

At stage $q$, outward-round the rational points $1/3$ and $2/3$ to
dyadic intervals $G_r$ at precision $p$. For each $r\in\{1/3,2/3\}$, charge the
child-call operation to the parent counter. If no parent work unit remains,
return inconclusive; otherwise pass the positive remaining budget as the
child's work cap and call
[[alg-certified-gamma-loggamma-evaluation]] with target $\Gamma$ on the
complex rectangle $G_r+i[0,0]$, absolute tolerance $2^{-q}$, no relative
tolerance, the same exponent range, fixed elementary truncation $q$,
base format precision $p$, and precision cap $p$. Debit every operation
performed by the Gamma child to the shared counter. A
success output rectangle encloses
$\Gamma(r)$, since $r\in G_r$; if either call is not successful or its
rectangle contains zero, skip this stage. A failed rational-to-dyadic conversion also makes the stage unavailable.

For $s\in\{1/6,1/3,2/3\}$, outward-round the exact rational $s$ to a
dyadic interval $S_{s,p}$, then call
[[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] on the real expression DAG
$\exp(S_{s,p}\log 3)$, with the same exponent range, precision $p$, and
truncation $q$. These calls enclose $3^s$ by
[[thm-real-elementary-range-enclosures]]. If a required call is not finite,
skip this stage. Embed each real power interval $X$ as the complex rectangle $X+i[0,0]$, then combine it with the Gamma rectangles by outward complex arithmetic
to enclose the two initial coefficients
$$(a_0,a_1)=\left(\frac{1}{3^{2/3}\Gamma(2/3)}, -\frac{1}{3^{1/3}\Gamma(1/3)}\right)$$
for Ai, or
$$(b_0,b_1)=\left(\frac{1}{3^{1/6}\Gamma(2/3)}, \frac{3^{1/6}}{\Gamma(1/3)}\right)$$
for Bi. If any divisor rectangle contains zero or an arithmetic operation is non-finite, skip this stage.

Put $R=|\Re z|+|\Im z|$, an exact rational upper bound for $|z|$.
For each residue $r=0,1$, initialize $t_{r,0}=c_r z^r$ using the
selected pair of initial coefficient intervals, and compute
$t_{r,j+1}=t_{r,j}z^3/((k+3)(k+2))$, where $k=r+3j$. Sum
$t_{r,0},\ldots,t_{r,q-1}$ and compute the first omitted term
$t_{r,q}$. Put $k_r=r+3q$ and
$$\rho_r=\frac{R^3}{(k_r+3)(k_r+2)}.$$
If either $\rho_r\ge1$, skip the stage. Otherwise enlarge the sum of both
partial rectangles in each coordinate by
$$\frac{M(t_{0,q})}{1-\rho_0}+\frac{M(t_{1,q})}{1-\rho_1},$$
where $M(X+iY)=\max(|\inf X|,|\sup X|)
+\max(|\inf Y|,|\sup Y|)$. The $c_2=0$ residue class vanishes identically.
The ratio and tail lemma [[lem-airy-series-coefficient-recurrence-and-tail]]
therefore makes the enlarged rectangle a containing enclosure of the selected
Airy value.

Round the final rectangle outward to precision $p$. Return success at the
first stage whose radius is at most $\varepsilon_a$. Set relative_certified
to true exactly when relative tolerance was requested, zero is excluded, and
the contract's relative-radius test passes; a failed relative test does not
prevent absolute success. If no stage succeeds before its caps, return
inconclusive. The stage loop and all subroutine calls have finite caps, so the
procedure has no unbounded retry.

## Definition

Input a nonnegative integer $M$, a finite dyadic interval $\mathcal T=[T_-,T_+]\subset[0,\infty)$, absolute tolerance $\varepsilon_a>0$, optional relative tolerance $\varepsilon_r>0$, a finite integer work cap $W$, a finite integer precision cap $P\ge2$, and a dyadic format with precision $2\le p\le P$, exponent bounds and elementary truncation index $K\ge1$. These are the backend parameters of [[def-certified-evaluation-result-contract]]. The output is a table of real dyadic intervals $I_m$ for $0\le m\le M$, with status `success`, `inconclusive`, `domain`, or `range`.

All arithmetic uses [[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]]. Every real elementary call means a typed DAG call to [[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] at the supplied format and fixed $K$. Embed an exact rational argument by outward rounding; check the domain of the entire rounded argument before calling. Square roots use the outward square-root operation. No machine elementary value is an endpoint certificate. Maintain a shared work counter: charge each arithmetic operation, conversion, comparison, loop update, summand and primitive child operation before executing it. Interrupt a child when the remaining counter reaches zero. A cap exhaustion or unresolved enclosure test gives `inconclusive`; a finite endpoint overflow gives `range`. Invalid original inputs give `domain`; a domain test obscured only by intermediate rounding gives `inconclusive`.

1. Validate the stated input conditions and supported format. Process the distinct endpoints in increasing order; process the distinct seed orders $m\in\{0,M\}$ in increasing order. At an endpoint $\tau=0$, form the exact rationals $1/(2m+1)$ for every $0\le m\le M$ and round them outward to the output format. Use this table without a recurrence. A rational is retained exactly internally, but a non-dyadic rational is not returned as a singleton dyadic interval.

2. For each positive endpoint $\tau$, perform refinements $k=0,1,\ldots,W-1$, subject to the shared work counter. At refinement $k$, try the two seed orders separately using their own $m$ and $s=m+\tfrac12$:

   - If $0<\tau\le1$, evaluate the Taylor polynomial through $N=k$ from [[thm-boys-integral-identities-series-and-incomplete-gamma]], then enlarge by the outward upper bound for $\tau^{N+1}/((N+1)!(2m+2N+3))$ from [[lem-boys-small-taylor-remainder]]. The condition $N+2\ge\tau$ holds throughout this branch.
   - If $1<\tau\le2m+1$, use $N=2^k$ panels of [[lem-boys-positive-midpoint-enclosure]], in increasing node order $j=1,\ldots,N$, and enlarge the positive midpoint sum by $(m+\tau)/(2N)$. Its dyadic nodes are formed exactly before storage; evaluate their exponentials by the finite real elementary call.
   - If $\tau>2m+1$, request the Gamma target from [[alg-certified-gamma-loggamma-evaluation]] on the exact rectangle $[s,s]+i[0,0]$, with child absolute tolerance $\varepsilon_a/2^{k+2}$, no relative request, base format precision $p_0=p$, the same exponent bounds and fixed elementary truncation $K$, child precision cap $P$, and child work cap $w=\lfloor R/4\rfloor$, where $R$ is the remaining parent work at call entry. If $w<1$, stop `inconclusive`. Debit its actual work, including unsuccessful work, to the parent counter. A successful child rectangle has real projection containing the real number $\Gamma(s)$: its reality follows from the positive-real Euler integral, also evaluated by the half-integer identity in [[thm-boys-integral-identities-series-and-incomplete-gamma]]. Use this projection as the real Gamma enclosure. Evaluate $e^{-\tau}$ by the real elementary call, and use [[lem-boys-incomplete-gamma-large-t-tail-bound]] to form the enclosing interval for $F_m(\tau)$. Compute $\tau^s=\tau^m\sqrt\tau$ and $\tau^{s-1}=\tau^s/\tau$ by outward operations; the exact denominator $1-\max(s-1,0)/\tau$ is positive. Replace a negative lower endpoint by zero, retaining the upper endpoint. A child `range` propagates `range`; a child `domain` on this valid positive argument or a child `inconclusive` invalidates that seed attempt and permits the next bounded refinement.

   A finite seed interval is available to its direction only when its radius is at most $\varepsilon_a$. A failed attempt does not invalidate a successfully enclosed seed for the other direction. Every panel and child loop is subject to the counter, even when its formal index bound is very large.

3. At each refinement obtain one finite real interval $J$ for $e^{-\tau}$. From an available order-zero seed form the upward candidate for orders $0,\ldots,M$; from an available order-$M$ seed form the downward candidate for orders $M,\ldots,0$. Use the exact affine recurrence maps in [[lem-boys-upward-downward-recurrence-error-amplification]]: compute each affine image's endpoints by exact rational endpoint arithmetic, then convert those two endpoints outward once. Record their two conversion errors and propagate the lemma's radius bounds, including half their sum at each step. This prescription avoids omitting rounding at intermediate nodes. A table is admissible only if every entry satisfies the propagated bound and the requested absolute and, if requested, zero-excluding relative-radius test. Keep the admissible candidate with smaller maximum radius, ties upward. If neither direction is admissible, continue to the next refinement. Once an endpoint table is chosen, proceed to the next endpoint. No upward division is attempted at zero.

4. With both endpoint tables, form $I_m=\operatorname{hull}(I_m(T_+),I_m(T_-))$ for every requested order, using endpoint minima and maxima. By $F'_m(T)=-F_{m+1}(T)<0$ from [[thm-boys-integral-identities-series-and-incomplete-gamma]], this encloses the full range over $\mathcal T$. Return `success` only after every output radius is at most $\varepsilon_a$ and, when relative tolerance is requested, the interval excludes zero and satisfies the relative-radius test in [[def-certified-evaluation-result-contract]]. Otherwise return `inconclusive`. Exhausting the finite refinement list or shared work counter also returns `inconclusive`. An unrepresentable finite output returns `range`. No branch promises success for every valid box or finite cap.

## Example

Take $\gamma=7/5$, density $\rho=10^{-8}$, pressure $p=10^{-12}$, and
velocities $u_L=-1/100$, $u_R=1/100$. The conserved states have
$m_{L,R}=\mp10^{-10}$ and $E_{L,R}=3\times10^{-12}$. Choose the symmetric HLL
speed $a=11/500$ at every face and Courant ratio $\nu=\Delta t/h=125/11$.
For the four-cell periodic data $(U_L,U_L,U_R,U_R)$, one HLL forward-Euler
update preserves positive density and pressure despite the very small initial
values. The calculation illustrates a first-order positivity branch; it does
not claim accuracy of the shock profile.

1.1 The kinetic energy density is $\rho u^2/2=5\times10^{-13}$ and $p/(\gamma-1)=5/2\times10^{-12}$, so $E=3\times10^{-12}$. Hence [F1] gives the specified pressure and positive internal energy, so both states lie in $\mathcal G_\gamma$. [given, F1, algebra]

## Statement

Use the exact data of
[[def-overlapping-schwarz-subspace-correction-data]], with one coarse space
$V_0$ and $m\ge1$ local spaces $V_1,\ldots,V_m$. Assume the stable-decomposition
and synthesis hypotheses of
[[thm-additive-schwarz-stable-decomposition-condition-number]] hold with
constants $C_0,C_1$. Suppose a symmetric matrix
$G=(\epsilon_{ij})_{i,j=1}^m$ has nonnegative entries and
$$ |a(v_i,v_j)|\le\epsilon_{ij}\|v_i\|_A\|v_j\|_A \quad(v_i\in V_i,\ v_j\in V_j). $$
For a real matrix $M$, write $\|M\|_2=\sup_{y\ne0}\|My\|_2/\|y\|_2$ for its
induced Euclidean operator norm. Set $\rho=\|G\|_2$ and
$K=1+2C_1+2(1+\rho)^2$. For the coarse-first exact multiplicative sweep
$E_{\mathrm{mult}}=(I-\Pi_m)\cdots(I-\Pi_1)(I-\Pi_0)$,
$$ \|E_{\mathrm{mult}}\|_A^2 \le 1-\frac{1}{C_0K}<1. $$
The ordered factors need not commute. Here
$\|S\|_A=\sup_{x\ne0}\|Sx\|_A/\|x\|_A$ is the induced operator norm.

1.1 For an arbitrary initial error $x$, set $e_{-1}=x$, $d_0=\Pi_0x$, and $e_0=x-d_0$. For $i=1,\ldots,m$, set $d_i=\Pi_i e_{i-1}$ and $e_i=e_{i-1}-d_i$. By [F2], each correction is orthogonal to its updated error, so telescoping gives $D:=\sum_{i=0}^m\|d_i\|_A^2 =\|x\|_A^2-\|e_m\|_A^2.$ Also $e_{i-1}=x-d_0-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1}d_j$. [F1, F2, given, construct]
cases.reason: The hypotheses require at least one local space in addition to the coarse space.

## Statement

Assume the model of [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]], all subdomain vertices primal, and the coefficient-scaled average of [[def-pe26-scaled-averaging-and-bddc-preconditioner]]. Let $P:=I-R E_0$ be the complementary jump projection on $\widetilde W$, and let $\|\cdot\|_{\widetilde S}$ be the energy norm induced by the partially assembled Schur operator. Then

$$\|Pw\|_{\widetilde S}^2\le C(1+\log(H/h))^2\|w\|_{\widetilde S}^2\qquad(w\in\widetilde W),$$

where $C$ depends only on the polygon/mesh shape bounds and bounded side count. It is independent of coefficient jumps, mesh size, subdomain diameter, and subdomain count.

1.1 Fix an open edge $E_{ij}$ and let $U_i=H_iw_i$, $U_j=H_jw_j$ be the local discrete harmonic extensions. Write $e_i=w_i^TS_iw_i=\rho_i\|\nabla U_i\|_{L^2(\Omega_i)}^2$ and similarly for $e_j$, by harmonic minimality and the definition of $S_i$. The $i$-copy of $Pw$ has nodal values $\alpha_j(w_i-w_j)$ at interior edge nodes and zero at its primal endpoints, so it is $I_h(\theta_E\alpha_j(w_i-w_j))$; the $j$-copy has the complementary coefficient $\alpha_i$. The $00,E$ norm controls the full boundary seminorm of an edge trace extended by zero off $E$: the cross-edge integrals are bounded by the endpoint weight in that norm, with constants uniform for the polygon angles and side count. Thus the trace-Schur upper bound [F3] applies to these supported traces. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]]. The elementwise trace map $\Gamma_0:H^1_0(\Omega)\to\prod_KH^1(K)/H^1_0(K)$ and normal-trace map $\Gamma_n:H(div;\Omega)\to\prod_K(H^1(K)/H^1_0(K))'$ have real Hilbert quotient ranges with global lift infimum norms. These equal the infima over broken extensions whose gluing belongs to the respective global space. Compatibility means membership in these ranges, so normal traces are conservative on each interior facet in the weak distributional sense.

1.1 H1 is complete: completeness of real $L^{2}$ [F6] gives limits in $L^{2}$ of a Cauchy sequence and each weak derivative satisfy distributional derivative identities by testing against compactly supported smooth functions and passing both integrals to their limits. H1_0 is closed by its closure definition. The scalar trace-quotient map is continuous because $\|[u|_K]\|_{H^1(K)/H^1_0(K)}\le\|u|_K\|_{H^1(K)}$ on each cell; the finite product preserves continuity. The normal map is continuous by [F2], again with a finite product. Thus both kernels are closed. [A1, F1, F2, F5, F6, F7, algebra]

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]]. The elementwise trace map $\Gamma_0:H^1_0(\Omega)\to\prod_KH^1(K)/H^1_0(K)$ and normal-trace map $\Gamma_n:H(div;\Omega)\to\prod_K(H^1(K)/H^1_0(K))'$ have real Hilbert quotient ranges with global lift infimum norms. These equal the infima over broken extensions whose gluing belongs to the respective global space. Compatibility means membership in these ranges, so normal traces are conservative on each interior facet in the weak distributional sense.

1.2 Let $\tau\in H(\operatorname{div};\Omega)$ and let an interior facet $F=K_+\cap K_-$ be fixed. For $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\operatorname{relint}F)$, choose a smooth function $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ supported in a small tubular neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}\psi$ meeting only $K_+$ and $K_-$ and having trace $\psi$ on $F$. The global distributional-divergence identity [F8] gives $\int_\Omega(\tau\cdot\nabla\phi+(\operatorname{div}\tau)\phi)=0$. Applying the cell Green identity [F2] to the two restrictions, with all other cell traces zero, yields $$\langle\gamma_{n_+,K_+}(\tau|_{K_+}),[\phi|_{K_+}]\rangle+\langle\gamma_{n_-,K_-}(\tau|_{K_-}),[\phi|_{K_-}]\rangle=0.$$ The two cell trace classes in this equation restrict to the same $\psi$ on $F$ and vanish on the other facets. Since this holds for every such $\psi$, the two outward weak normal traces cancel as distributions on the relative interior of each interior facet. This is the conservative facet relation for a global H(div) lift; it uses the distributional divergence identity and weak Green formula, not pointwise normal values. [F2, F8, given, construct, algebra]

## Statement

Assume full AC conservatively for the declared Hilbert projection dependencies. Let $X=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\subset\Omega$ be distinct and nonempty, and let $\mathcal H_k(\Omega)$ be the restricted Matérn native RKHS. For every $f\in\mathcal H_k(\Omega)$, the unique kernel interpolant $s_Xf=\sum_jc_jk(\cdot-x_j)$ is the orthogonal projection of $f$ onto $V_X=\operatorname{span}\{k(\cdot-x_j):1\le j\le N\}$. Define
$$P_X(x)=\|(I-\Pi_X)k(\cdot-x)\|_{\mathcal H_k(\Omega)},$$
where $\Pi_X$ is that projection. Then for every $x\in\Omega$,
$$|f(x)-s_Xf(x)|\le P_X(x)\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k(\Omega)},\qquad P_X(x)^2=k(0)-k_X(x)^*K_X^{-1}k_X(x)\ge0.$$
where $K_X=(k(x_i-x_j))$ and $k_X(x)=(k(x_i-x))_{i=1}^N$.

1.1 The span $V_X$ has finite dimension and is therefore closed. Let $\Pi_Xf$ be the orthogonal projection of $f$ onto $V_X$. For each site $x_i$, the residual is orthogonal to $k(\cdot-x_i)$; by reproduction [F1], $(f-\Pi_Xf)(x_i)=0$. Thus $\Pi_Xf$ interpolates the data. Its coefficients solve $K_Xc=(f(x_i))_i$, which has a unique solution by [F2], so it is the unique kernel interpolant. [F1, F2, F3, A1]

## Statement

Assume full AC conservatively for the declared Hilbert projection dependencies. Let $X=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\subset\Omega$ be distinct and nonempty, and let $\mathcal H_k(\Omega)$ be the restricted Matérn native RKHS. For every $f\in\mathcal H_k(\Omega)$, the unique kernel interpolant $s_Xf=\sum_jc_jk(\cdot-x_j)$ is the orthogonal projection of $f$ onto $V_X=\operatorname{span}\{k(\cdot-x_j):1\le j\le N\}$. Define
$$P_X(x)=\|(I-\Pi_X)k(\cdot-x)\|_{\mathcal H_k(\Omega)},$$
where $\Pi_X$ is that projection. Then for every $x\in\Omega$,
$$|f(x)-s_Xf(x)|\le P_X(x)\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k(\Omega)},\qquad P_X(x)^2=k(0)-k_X(x)^*K_X^{-1}k_X(x)\ge0.$$
where $K_X=(k(x_i-x_j))$ and $k_X(x)=(k(x_i-x))_{i=1}^N$.

1.1 The span $V_X$ has finite dimension and is therefore closed. Let $\Pi_Xf$ be the orthogonal projection of $f$ onto $V_X$. For each site $x_i$, the residual is orthogonal to $k(\cdot-x_i)$; by reproduction [F1], $(f-\Pi_Xf)(x_i)=0$. Thus $\Pi_Xf$ interpolates the data. Its coefficients solve $K_Xc=(f(x_i))_i$, which has a unique solution by [F2], so it is the unique kernel interpolant. [F1, F2, F3, A1]

## Statement

Assume full AC conservatively for the Hilbert projection and weighted-$L^2$ suppliers. Fix arbitrary $d\ge1$, $
u>0$, $a>0$, $s=
u+d/2$, the normalized Matérn kernel $k$ of [[def-normalized-matern-spectral-kernel]], and an admitted uniform-cone domain $\Omega$. There are constants $C,h_0>0$, depending only on $d,
u,a$ and the domain's cone constants, such that for every finite nonempty distinct site set $X\subset\Omega$ with fill distance $h_X\le h_0$ and every $f\in H^s(\Omega)$,
$$\|f-s_Xf\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\le C h_X^
u\|f\|_{H^s(\Omega)},\qquad \sup_{x\in\Omega}P_X(x)\le C h_X^
u.$$
Here $s_Xf$ and $P_X$ are the native interpolant and power function of [[thm-native-interpolation-projection-and-power-function]]. The rate requires no mesh-ratio bound. The constants are uniform over site sets satisfying the fill-distance condition.

1.1 By [F4] choose an integer $m>
u$ and apply the zeros estimate [F2] with this fixed $m$. Regard $f$ as an element of the same set of continuous restrictions $H^s(\Omega)=\mathcal H_k(\Omega)$ using [F1], and let $e=f-s_Xf$. By [F3], $e|_X=0$ and $\|e\|_{\mathcal H_k(\Omega)}\le\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k(\Omega)}$. Therefore [F1] and [F2] give $$\|e\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\le C_0h_X^
u\|e\|_{H^s(\Omega)}\le C_0c^{-1}h_X^
u\|e\|_{\mathcal H_k(\Omega)}\le C_0c^{-1}C_1h_X^
u\|f\|_{H^s(\Omega)}.$$ This is the first estimate. [F1, F2, F3, F4, A1, algebra]

u\|f\|_{H^s(\Omega)},\qquad \sup_{x\in\Omega}P_X(x)\le C h_X^
u.$$
Here $s_Xf$ and $P_X$ are the native interpolant and power function of [[thm-native-interpolation-projection-and-power-function]]. The rate requires no mesh-ratio bound. The constants are uniform over site sets satisfying the fill-distance condition.

2.1 Fix $x\in\Omega$ and set $r_x=(I-\Pi_X)k(\cdot-x)$, so $P_X(x)=\|r_x\|$. Self-adjointness and reproduction in [F3] give $f(x)-s_Xf(x)=\langle f,r_x\rangle$. The bound in [F3] shows that this residual evaluation functional has norm at most $P_X(x)$. If $r_x=0$, it is the zero functional and its norm is $P_X(x)=0$. If $r_x\ne0$, the unit vector $f_x=r_x/\|r_x\|$ satisfies $f_x(x)-s_Xf_x(x)=\langle f_x,r_x\rangle=\|r_x\|=P_X(x)$, so the functional norm is exactly $P_X(x)$. Applying step 1.1 to every $f$ of native norm at most one therefore gives $P_X(x)\le C_2h_X^\nu$, uniformly in $x$; taking the supremum proves the second estimate. The constant does not depend on $X$ except through the upper bound on $h_X$, and no mesh ratio entered either [F2] or this argument. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a bounded connected Lipschitz polygonal/polyhedral domain in dimension $d=2$ or $3$, with a conforming shape-regular simplicial mesh family of mesh size $h$. Put $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$ and $Q=L^2_0(D)$. For $\nu>0$ and $F\in V'$, suppose $(u,p)\in V\times Q$ satisfies
$$2\nu\int_D\varepsilon(u):\varepsilon(v)-\int_Dp\,\operatorname{div}v=F(v),\qquad -\int_Dq\,\operatorname{div}u=0$$
for every $v\in V,q\in Q$, with $u\in H^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$ and $p\in H^1(D)$. Let $(u_h,p_h)\in V_h\times Q_h$ solve the same equations for every $v_h\in V_h,q_h\in Q_h$, where $V_h,Q_h$ are the P1-bubble/P1 mini spaces. Then
$$\|u-u_h\|_{H^1(D)}+\|p-p_h\|_{L^2(D)}\le C h(\|u\|_{H^2(D)}+\|p\|_{H^1(D)}).$$

Assume Countable Choice and the MINI mesh hypotheses. For $z\in V_\sigma$, define $S_hz\in Z_h$ by
$$a_\nu(S_hz,w_h)=a_\nu(z,w_h)\qquad(w_h\in Z_h).$$
This defines a unique linear projection and
$$\|z-S_hz\|_V\le\sqrt2\inf_{w_h\in Z_h}\|z-w_h\|_V.$$
If additionally $z\in H^2(D)^d$ and $q\in H^1(D)\cap L^2_0(D)$, then
$$\|z-S_hz\|_V\le C_0(1+\nu^{-1})h\bigl(\|z\|_{H^2(D)}+\|q\|_{H^1(D)}\bigr),$$
where $C_0$ is independent of $h$ and $\nu$ and depends on $D$, shape regularity and the uniform MINI inf-sup constant.
